h: How to Win (or at Least Not Come Last)
p: Every group has its strategies, but a few general tips can help you climb the leaderboard. First, watch the room carefully before diving in. Most challenges have a pattern or rhythm, and spotting it early saves you from flailing about. Second, decide on roles. Some rooms reward one fast runner, others need everyone working in sync, so play to each person's strengths.

Third, don't burn out early. It's tempting to go all-out in the first room, but six rooms is a decent workout, and you'll want something left in the tank for the last one. Grab some water between rounds and keep the banter going, because laughing at each other's mishaps is half the experience.

Boom Lab is ideal for celebrations because it creates instant stories. Everyone will remember the moment the most competitive person in the group tripped over a laser beam or the youngest beat the grown-ups. For birthday parties, it's a good idea to arrange some food afterwards so everyone can refuel and relive the highlights.

For families, it's worth checking any age or height guidance before booking, as some challenges are quite physical. Older kids and teens usually get the most out of it, and it's the kind of activity that gets screen-loving teenagers off the sofa without them even noticing they're exercising. Adults shouldn't underestimate it either. You'll likely be surprised how competitive you get once the scoreboard lights up.

As with any London day out, give yourself time to get there, especially at busy weekends when trains and Tubes can be packed. And once you've finished, there's no shortage of places to celebrate your victory or plot your revenge for next time.
